Hola, buen día.

Para empezar por lo bueno, el juego tiene una estética muy agradable, tanto por los colores como por el diseño de los personajes y enemigos, lo que representa una mejora respecto al juego flash original.

Otra cosa que pulieron en esta reinvención es el combate. En el primer juego se sentía algo tosco por momentos, al punto de que quedarse quieto era prácticamente una sentencia de muerte. En cambio, acá el combate es más permisivo y se puede pelear cuerpo a cuerpo sin tanto riesgo frente a enemigos comunes.

Algo que no terminé de entender y que me pareció un añadido poco relevante es el álbum de stickers. Si fueran elementos propios del juego, o incluso diseños del juego flash original como guiño, estaría bien. Pero incluye referencias a otros juegos y compañías (como Hollow Knight), lo que se siente bastante fuera de lugar. Como coleccionable no está mal, pero creo que podrían haberlo aprovechado mejor.

Por otro lado, una pega real del juego es la monotonía del gameplay. Después de aproximadamente una hora se vuelve repetitivo, al punto de que tenía que dejar de jugar un rato porque la experiencia era siempre la misma. No arruina el juego, pero sí afecta el ritmo.

En resumen: es una buena reinvención del juego flash. Aunque personalmente me sigue gustando más el original, mantiene bien su esencia y la adapta para llegar a un público nuevo. Lo recomiendo para jugar una vez, especialmente si te gustó la versión flash.

I first played The Adventure Pals years ago on the Nintendo Switch, and picking it up again during Steam’s winter sale reminded me why I loved it in the first place. This game is pure joy — a colorful, silly, wonderfully absurd platformer that never takes itself too seriously.

The controls are smooth and intuitive, the art style is bright and charming, and the characters are delightfully weird in all the right ways. The Adventure Pals leans fully into bizarre humor, and it works beautifully. One moment you’re helping a farmer find his missing “bride,” only to discover she’s actually a pig. He’s thrilled, thanks you profusely, and promises to treat you to bacon next time. That’s the kind of energy this game runs on.

The main villain is equally ridiculous, kidnapping elderly people to turn them into hot dogs. Throughout the adventure you’ll fight angry hot dogs in buns, and when you defeat them, they transform back into old folks. It’s strange, it’s silly, and it’s consistently entertaining.

The soundtrack deserves a shout‑out too — upbeat, catchy, and perfectly matched to the game’s cheerful chaos.

In short, The Adventure Pals is a wonderfully fun platformer packed with personality. It’s lighthearted, imaginative, and simply a great time. Whether you’re revisiting it or discovering it for the first time, it’s hard not to smile while playing.

I came across this game when I was a kid playing the former flash game "super adventure pals" and also by watching DanTDM's playthrough of it. Back then it seemed incredibly fun and seemed so cool.... I was wrong. The level of mediocrity in this game is completely unmatched. 

When you first begin to play the game it seems fun, there's a lot to do: a shop , a level up system , items you can use, cards to collect, and even accessories. However you level up incredibly fast in this game so by the time you're halfway through the game you're already max level. Although each level up does some quality of life improvements it's overall ruined by having barely any use. For example you have a rock as a pal and a skill you unlock is it's ability to do chain attacks. This little midget rock does these chain attacks once in a blue moon. It's like in anime when the main character fights the villain and the villain practically puts the mc in a vegetative state and only then do the side characters decide to join in and help. Why must I wait until I've gone through 4 health potions to finally be aided by some little turd looking rock? The accessories are cool but why does the pathetic stone get the cool looking stuff and my giraffe gets absolutely nothing?

Each level consists of 5 stages of which there is 1 muffin to collect for each stage as well as a card that is randomly across either one of the 5 stages. Then while playing through each level you realise how boring and monotonous each one becomes. There's no linear path to literally most levels. So you spend time circling back to places you have already been while attempting to get these muffins and cards and it makes you feel like you're in some sort of mental asylum living the same day over and over again. 

As you progress it's almost as if the developers just realised how much they really dgaf, they genuinely use the same creatures  disguised as different animals and call it a day. It's like in mario if you were to finish the grasslands biome having gone against goompas and koopa troopas , and then in the ice biome you just go against the same exact same goompas and koopa troopas but instead the developers just redesigned them as polar bears and arctic foxes. It's just a cop out and embarrassing. Also while searching for muffins you might accidentally go to the portal well (which is where the end of each stage is) and instead of being able to just walk back (to get the muffin) you have to become prime ♥♥♥♥ Grayson (Nightwing) and do some next acrobatics to get out. And if you were to miss the muffin you would have to restart the stage again at a later point.

However at the time of writing this review, I still am playing this game and the only thing motivating me is unlocking all achievements. That's it. Literally every level past the first biome requires you to do some goofy unnecessary puzzle because the developers thought that it would make the game more fun. Hello? 

All in all, I understand this is a kids game but I am utterly disappointed from how blinded I was by nostalgia. If you are a masochist by all means play this game.

It's fun game that tries different things in it's gameplay loop. Story is stupid but it's fun in the way it's telling and in it's humor. It doesn't take itself too seriously. Made me laugh in some spots. Gameplay loop is kind of boring/repetitive as you smack opponents until they or you die. The game has extras as different bombs and healing items but in the end I used only the healing items as they were easier to use than cycling trough items to use (rather than press two buttons and thinking, I just used health potions). But I was addicted to collecting collectables. In the end I collected all muffins and stickers*. Had fun with the story and the levels. Levels mostly were straight forward and you could tell where the secrets were hidden. Also throughout the game there were more aspects to different levels a.i. swinging and underwater sections that broke the mold and made the game more fun.
In the end I wanted to fully complete the game but in early game there was two decisions that locked me out of it. One related to a whale having wrong pants and One with the elections. So if you want to 100% this game then keep in the mind that you have to make two right decisions that can lock your achievements (for legal reasons I have to say I didn't search a way do undo these mistakes).
I recommend this game to somebody who like platformers or to someone who wants to play with their children because it's on the easier side and easy to learn. It took me 3 evenings to beat.
